Why does falciparum malaria cause cerebral malaria?
Infected red cells stick to the walls of small vessels (sequestration).
Why do vivax and ovale malaria relapse?
Because of dormant forms in the liver (hypnozoites).
Which red cell condition protects against severe falciparum malaria?
What is the gold standard test for malaria?
A thick and thin blood film.
How does a thick film differ from a thin film?
The thick film finds and counts the parasites; the thin film identifies the species.
What does falciparum malaria look like on the thin film?
Small rings, often several in one red cell, and banana-shaped gametocytes.
What is the limitation of the HRP2 rapid diagnostic test?
It stays positive for weeks after treatment.
What are the clinical features of severe malaria?
Impaired consciousness, prostration, more than 2 convulsions in 24 hours, respiratory distress, shock, bleeding and jaundice.
What are the laboratory features of severe malaria?
Glucose below 2.2 mmol/L, haemoglobin below 5 g/dL, lactate of 5 mmol/L or more, kidney injury and a parasitaemia above 10%.
What is the first bedside test in a comatose child with malaria?
What is the first-line drug for uncomplicated falciparum malaria?
Artemether–lumefantrine, 6 doses over 3 days, taken with food.
How many tablets of artemether–lumefantrine does a 12 kg child take per dose?
One tablet per dose (the dose for 5–14 kg).
What is the second-line artemisinin combination therapy?
What is the drug of choice for severe malaria?
What is the dose of artesunate for children under and over 20 kg?
3 mg/kg for children under 20 kg; 2.4 mg/kg for children of 20 kg or more.
What is the schedule of artesunate in severe malaria?
At 0, 12 and 24 hours, then daily, for at least 24 hours and until the child can take oral treatment; then a full course of artemisinin combination therapy.
What pre-referral treatment is given to a young child with severe malaria?
Rectal artesunate 10 mg/kg, in children under 6 years.
What is used if artesunate is not available?
Intramuscular artemether, or quinine (a loading dose of 20 mg/kg, then 10 mg/kg 8-hourly).
When is blood transfused in malaria?
When the haemoglobin is below 4 g/dL, or below 6 g/dL with respiratory distress or shock.
How is the radical cure of vivax malaria given?
Primaquine 0.25–0.5 mg/kg daily for 14 days, after a G6PD test.
At what age is the malaria vaccine given, and how many doses?
RTS,S or R21 from 5 months of age, in 4 doses.
